stories.headline: Russian strike on Kyiv arms depot kills dozens and sparks wide evacuations
stories.body:
Russian drones struck a Ukrainian military ammunition depot near Kyiv on Friday night. The BBC reported that 37 people died, while Al Jazeera reported 38 people died. The BBC said that 42 people were injured, including four children. Al Jazeera said that dozens of people were wounded. The explosion happened in the Bucha district on the outskirts of Kyiv. The warehouse was in Myla and belonged to the Ukrainian military. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed that the depot stored shells, drones, and other munitions. The strike caused stored shells, mines, and drones to explode late on Friday. More than 370 people were evacuated from the surrounding area. The BBC said almost 400 people were evacuated.

The explosions damaged a care home for elderly and disabled people. Tymur Tkachenko, head of the local regional military administration, said the strike started a fire that damaged at least 50 residential buildings. Ukrainian media cited Tkachenko as saying 34 of the victims were residents at the care facility. Taras Didych, head of the Dmytrivka community, died while trying to rescue others during the explosion. Russia's Ministry of Defence said its forces targeted an ammunition depot containing launch boosters and drone parts.

Ukrainian leaders criticized the decision to store weapons near homes. President Zelensky said storing explosives next to residential areas was terrible negligence. He said criminal proceedings had been opened. Ukrainian Prime Minister Sergiy Koretsky said repeating storage mistakes in the fifth year of the full-scale invasion is criminal negligence. This was the second strike on a Kyiv munitions depot in less than two months. An earlier strike hit an ammunition warehouse in Vyshneve in July. The BBC said that July explosion killed nine people, injured dozens, and damaged over 280 homes. Prime Minister Koretsky said 22 people died in that July attack. An investigation showed a state-owned company broke rules about storing explosives near homes. President Zelensky said two officials from state-owned companies, including arms maker Ukroboronprom, would be held accountable for illegal storage.

Attacks hit other regions as well. Kyiv Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko said a two-year-old child died after a Russian drone crashed in Obolonskyi. Regional administration head Oleksandr Prokudin said Russian strikes on Kherson on Saturday killed two people and wounded 27 others. The Ukrainian army said it shot down 233 Russian drones overnight. Pavlo Palisa, deputy head of Ukraine's presidential office, said Ukrainian interceptor drones are not yet effective enough against jet-powered Russian drones. President Zelensky said Ukraine aims to launch 1,000 long-range drone strikes on Russia every day.

stories.headline: Niger military moves to stop army mutiny in capital city Niamey
stories.body:
Niger's military moved to stop a mutiny by rebel soldiers in the capital city of Niamey. Rebellious troops attacked military officers, held soldiers hostage at a barracks, and fired at key sites. Witnesses reported heavy gunfire and explosions at Base 101 shortly after midnight on Saturday. Rebel soldiers tried to enter the presidential palace and blocked the national television broadcaster Tele Sahel. The channel went off the air for just over an hour before resuming broadcasts around 10:00 a.m. local time.

Niger's defence ministry said armed forces were retaking control of targeted sites. Diplomatic and security sources said the presidential guard, aided by Russian forces, recaptured an air base and killed several mutineers by Saturday evening. But regional sources said rebelling troops still held two barracks around Niamey on Saturday.

This mutiny was the third major incident at the capital's airport complex in 2026. Jihadists had previously attacked the airport twice earlier in the year. General Abdourahamane Tiani seized power in Niger in 2023, cutting ties with Western partners and aligning with Russia. Neighbouring Algeria condemned the mutiny and offered support to Niger's government.

A group of soldiers in Niger rebelled against officers at a military base and fired at sensitive locations across Niamey.

Tele Sahel went off the air for just over an hour after soldiers blocked access to the station, before restoring broadcasts around 10:00 a.m. local time.
State television station Tele Sahel resumed broadcasting on Saturday after temporarily going offline during the unrest in Niamey.
Niger's defence ministry stated on state television that armed forces were progressively retaking control of sites targeted in an overnight attack on Niamey.
Diplomatic and security sources reported that Niger's presidential guard, assisted by Russian forces, recaptured an air base in Niamey and killed several mutineers by Saturday evening.
Regional security and African diplomatic sources stated that rebelling troops still held two barracks around Niamey on Saturday.
The mutiny in Niamey marked the third major instance of unrest at the capital's airport complex in 2026.
Niamey airport was attacked twice by jihadists earlier in 2026, first by Islamic State in the Sahel in January and later in late June by the Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims.
General Abdourahamane Tiani seized power in Niger in 2023, subsequently severing ties with Western partners and strengthening ties with Russia.
The government of neighbouring Algeria condemned the mutiny in Niamey and pledged support for the Nigerien government.

stories.headline: Rescuers search for thousands after Himalayan flood disaster kills hundreds
stories.body:
Rescuers searched for thousands of missing people across Nepal, India, and China after massive flash floods. The US Geological Survey said a massive glacial collapse caused the high-altitude disaster, sending debris torrents downstream. The confirmed death toll reached 682 people, including 675 in Nepal and seven in Tibet. Disaster agencies said nearly 3,000 people are missing. This includes 2,426 missing people in Nepal and 554 in Tibet. The missing list includes at least 777 foreign nationals and 933 hydropower project workers. The Red Cross estimated that the disaster affected at least 93,000 people, while over 3,700 people were rescued in Nepal.

Rescue operations focused heavily on trapped workers. The Nepali army pumped air through pipes into tunnels at the Trishuli 3A and 3B hydropower sites. Nepalese Energy Minister Biraj Bhakta Shrestha said workers drilled a hole into a cable tunnel, but could not reach trapped staff. Nepal asked for specialized foreign help, including tunnel rescue teams, tracking tech, DNA analysis tools, and mortuary facilities. India sent an 11-member technical team for tunnel rescue, and a Chinese team was expected soon.

Several countries took action to aid victims and locate citizens. Indian authorities said they rescued 88 Indian nationals in Nepal, including four hydropower workers in Rasuwa. India's Ministry of External Affairs reduced its figure of missing Indian citizens in Nepal to 287 on Saturday. The ministry said another 128 uncontactable people in Nepal were of Indian origin with other nationalities. On Saturday, 120 Indian nationals crossed from Tibet into Nepal. In Tibet, Chinese authorities at Gyirong port evacuated 555 tourists and moved 499 local residents and workers to safety. Chinese monitors confirmed that a dammed debris lake started draining naturally, reducing immediate flood risks.

The international response and climate concerns drew attention. The US State Department promised $500,000 in initial emergency aid for Nepal. Nepalese Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi agreed to share satellite and water data in real time. Khanal noted that Nepal produces only about 0.01 percent of global greenhouse gas emissions despite facing severe impacts. UN climate chief Simon Stiell said burning fossil fuels warms the climate and makes mountain disasters more frequent and severe. Meanwhile, flood survivors in Nuwakot district publicly criticized the Nepalese government for slow relief delivery and search efforts.

stories.headline: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat speaks at New York event amid local protests
stories.body:
RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat spoke at a diaspora event at Madison Square Garden in New York. He delivered the keynote address at the Universal Oneness Celebration, supported by over 200 Hindu American groups. Bhagwat said that if any Hindu believes Muslims should not live in India, that person is no longer a Hindu. He said RSS volunteers run about 130,000 service projects and increased dialogue with Muslim and Christian communities starting in 2018. To highlight equal service, he cited volunteer work after the 1996 Charkhi Dadri plane crash in Haryana.

Bhagwat arrived in the United States on Tuesday for a centenary outreach tour across North America and the UK. He also spoke to leaders at the One World, One Humanity conference on August 29.

The visit drew strong pushback. Civil rights, interfaith, and caste groups protested outside Madison Square Garden. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani opposed the event, calling the group's ideology exclusionary. The US Commission on International Religious Freedom recommended revoking Bhagwat's visa and sanctioning RSS members. Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi previously spoke to 50,000 people at a 2019 event in Texas.

The Universal Oneness Celebration at Madison Square Garden was supported by over 200 Hindu American organizations.

stories.headline: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrives in Uzbekistan for regional summit tour
stories.body:
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived in Uzbekistan on Saturday to start a two-nation Central Asian tour. Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev personally greeted Modi at Tashkent airport late at night. Modi's plane flew through Chinese airspace because Pakistan kept its airspace closed to Indian planes. This trip is Modi's fourth official visit to Uzbekistan, following visits in 2015, 2016, and 2022.

Modi said he plans to discuss trade, investment, defense, and energy with President Mirziyoyev. His schedule in Tashkent included visiting the Shastri Memorial, laying flowers at Yangi Uzbekistan Park, and visiting Tashkent State University. Uzbekistan hosts over 18,000 Indian residents, including about 16,000 medical students.

Modi will later attend the 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek and the World Nomad Games in Kyrgyzstan. India's Ministry of External Affairs said Modi will meet Russian President Vladimir Putin during the summit. The ten-nation group covers 36 million square kilometers and over 3.4 billion people. The bloc represents about 25 percent of global economic output and over 15 percent of world trade.

The SCO accounts for approximately 25 percent of global gross domestic product and over 15 percent of international trade.
